Yes, Chef

Grace Reilly

3.81
16,614 ratings4,767 reviews
Rate this book
The Bear meets It Happened One Summer in this delicious new romance from USA Today bestselling author Grace Reilly, in which a down-on-his-luck chef and a determined social media maven strike a reluctant deal to bring a beloved restaurant back to life.

If you can’t take the heat…get out of the kitchen.

After a public meltdown in the dining room of one of Manhattan’s most elite restaurants, Chef Jack Hartman is back in his South Florida hometown. Angry, grieving, and saddled with the unwanted storefront his late mentor left him, his life is spinning out of control. And that’s before Poppy Winfield, the blond, bubbly, utterly infuriating daughter of his former boss, shows up at his dock.

Poppy needs to escape. From her disapproving family, her horrible ex-boyfriend, and her reputation as someone who has never taken anything seriously. But more than that, she wants to prove herself—and she has just the plan to do it. Unfortunately, that plan involves Jack Hartman, the most arrogant, prickly, intimidating man she’s ever had the pleasure of throwing a shrimp at.

She knows Jack is desperate to come back from his unceremonious firing, so she proposes a deal: working together to open a revamped version of his mentor’s restaurant. He’ll handle the menu, and she’ll use her skill as a social media influencer to sell the hell out of its grand opening. If she and Jack can make the restaurant a success, it’ll be an accomplishment no one can deny—and a ticket for them both to return to New York.

Jack is intrigued, but only on his terms: if Poppy’s going to work for him, she must learn the ropes of the entire business. Including how to cook. From him.

As sparks fly both in and out of the kitchen and tensions reach a boiling point, Poppy and Jack are left wondering--could they be a perfect pairing? Or is this whole experiment a recipe for disaster?

About the author

Grace Reilly

8 books4,330 followers
Hi! I’m Grace.

I’m so glad you’re here! Originally from Long Island, I now live in Florida, where I pretend the lizards in my backyard are miniature dragons and soak up the sunshine. I can usually be found with a notebook in one hand and a paperback (or my Kindle!) in another. A storyteller at heart with a deep romantic streak, I write what I love to read: stories filled with swoon and steam, laughter and love, family and friendships, and authentic, earnest emotions and growth. I love drawing on my personal passions for my books, which is how my sports fanaticism resulted in the Beyond the Play series.

More about me: I collect earrings, the quirkier the better. I never turn down a good mint chocolate chip ice cream. I listen to way too much sports talk radio. And I adore writing about couples who are stronger together.

Review of advance copy received from NetGalley
April 7, 2026
˗ˏˋ ꒰ 🥭 ꒱ ˎˊ˗ 5 𝒔𝒕𝒂𝒓𝒔 ✰

╰┈➤ ❝ She's ridiculous. Ridiculously charming. Ridiculously pretty. Ridiculously magnetic, from her halo of hair down to her delicate ankles.❞

Am I overexaggerating? Or do I think I just found the romance book for the summer. As a longtime admirer of Grace Reilly's work, it is undeniable that her writing is sheer magic. I was captured by the immediate tension between Poppy and Jack. From the moment they met, they were unexplainably drawn to each other but at the same time were at each other's throats and I loved it.

˗ˏˋ ꒰ 🌊 ꒱ ˎˊ ˗ 𝒕𝒓𝒐𝒑𝒆𝒔:

🍍Grumpy x Sunshine
🍍Enemies to lovers
🍍Chef x Influencer
🍍Small town
🍍Boss's Daughter


Poppy, a lifestyle influencer, who, despite her millions of followers and multiple brand deals, struggles to find approval from her seemingly perfect and successful family.

Jack, despite being a esteemed Chef drowns under the weight of Sal's death, his mentor and father figure. After an unfortunate night where Jack gets fired from the high end restaurant, and Poppy gets broken up with, Poppy and Jack form a tentative friendship. That doesn't last long though. Jack returns to fix up Sal's restaurant the Sailfish, but there's one problem, he needs visibility and marketing if he's going to salvage the poor place. That's where Poppy comes in, despite her help being quite unwanted by Jack.

This creates the most electric enemies to lovers arc. Forced proximity in a kitchen that's practically falling apart, teaching Poppy how to cook on a line, and a magnetic attraction between them that's bound to implode at any moment. This was so entertaining to read, I was kicking my feet and giggling at some of Poppy and Jack's interactions.

Now, let's talk vibes: one word, immaculate. So fun and Summery, I wouldn't be surprised if this ended up being the book of the Summer. I mean seriously, you can't beat the Florida atmosphere and the heat of the kitchen in the mist of dinner service. This book was marketed as It Happened One Summer meets The Bear. While I haven't read The Bear, I can certainly confirm that the vibes of this book and Tessa Bailey's book are identical in their small-town charm. Not to mention that Poppy is also an influencer who comes from a big city and is dropped into a small town. The only difference is that, Poppy is such a likable main character. I admire her tenacity and her willingness to not give up. It made it easy and enjoyable to root for her.

Throughout this book, I was generally charmed by Jack. My only problem was his tenancy to be a jerk to Poppy. I know that was part of his character arc, but I really do not like to root for a male lead who is rude to the female main character. I get being rude in the beginning, but I felt as though he was too rude at times even towards the end of the book. That's not to say he was all bad, there were definitely some things to appreciate. Like the tattoos?!! Hello? He was such a hot bad boy chef. Also, after Poppy and him started getting along, he was endlessly patient when teaching her the basics of cooking and the science behind it.

I'd like to take a quick moment to acknowledge the amazing side characters. Kiara and Chester added so much life in this book. I was as invested in their little side plot as I was in the main love story.

To conclude, I think that this book is absolute gold. Reilly does an amazing job on all the character work and the setting and vibes and everything in between. If you’re looking for your summer romance—this is it. ☀️

⭐️ 4.5 ⭐️ As someone who has a love/hate relationship with rom-coms and contemporary romances, Yes, Chef was delicious. It was better than I expected! I am a huge fan of food-centric settings and this book definitely delivered on the hunger, pun intended. It had great plot, great ADHD rep, character development, fantastic banter, loads of funny scenes that had me laughing out loud. Oh and let's not forget the spice, tension and their magnetic energy was all chefs kiss! Add this to your list you will not be disappointed!

Chef Jack Hartmann has had it rough. His life has been tough the last couple of years and he's grumpy, angry..and he just got fired from his job. Poppy, the bubbly ray of sunshine, is never enough for her family and has grown up in the shadows of her sister's success..annnddd she was just publicly broken up with in the very same restaurant where Jack works. After a very public meltdown, Jack leaves off to South Florida and Poppy has a plan to prove herself and that plan involves Jack Hartmann. They agree to work together on a restaurant that has been handed off to Jack after his mentors passing. Jack is to handle the menu, Poppy is to handle the social success--with them working together, what can possibly go wrong? They low-key sort of hate one another but are forced to proximity from the very start. As sparks begin to fly, the kitchen is burning up and a masterpiece begins to flourish.

My goodness, this was so good. I can't believe I'm saying this, but this book just entered by top 10 books for contemporary reads for this year. I always look out for emotional depth (a big must!) and meaningful conversations in contemporary romances because for me to really enjoy a romance or rom-com, it needs to be light, heartfelt and something that speaks to me. Yes, Chef was all of that and much more--poignant, relatable, sizzling hot! I liked how different yet the same both love interests were. Jack had a rough exterior shaped by turbulent childhood while Poppy has been let down too many times to count. Her father didn't believe in her hard work and grind, despite being a well established influencer. Both faced many setbacks than gains and yet wanted to prove something, first and foremost to themselves. Poppy's insecurities felt very real and valid. A lot of women can relate to what she was going through. Jack's ADHD representation was also very well done and I loved how he used his kitchen, his love for cooking as a self-soothing mechanism to cope with his personal struggles. Together, they elevated each other and had frank conversations that helped them work through their personal friction and fears.

The spice was definitely spicing in this book. Their magnetism was sizzling hot, like 3-4 chili peppers hot. I loved how food-centric this book was and how it just made things more steamier. Being in the kitchen, cooking together, exploring ingredients and each other, talk about the heat! Honestly, don't hesitate to pick this one up, it's going to make you hungry. The food thats described in this book was seriously mouth watering.

Nothing but praise for the narrators because they really brought two voices to life and I too can tell, they were having fun while narrating this story!

— Rating: 4 ★ .ᐟ

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎‎ I am beyond glad that I picked this book back up after my initial DNF because it was ten times more enjoyable when reading it during the summer! Yes, Chef is definitely not for everyone and I can recognize the aspects that may be why certain people didn’t like it, but for me I was completely immersed in the story. Whenever I had to put this book down, I was longing to pick it up again because I was so invested in Poppy and Jack’s relationship. This book wasn’t anything extraordinary, it didn’t have any life-changing or emotionally destroying moments, but it was so entertaining that it kept me utterly addicted to the plot and romance.

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎‎ Now, I haven’t read many romance books, but I felt that this one had such a unique plot! Seeing both main characters work together despite their differences to build up a practically abandoned restaurant was so interesting. I was completely invested in their journey, flipping each page with excitement to see what the restaurant would become once they were finished. The other plot lines were just as entertaining, like the cooking lessons that had such descriptive writing it made me hungry. Obviously there were some downsides, like the rather repetitive points in the book that occurred after the main characters had officiated a friend’s with benefits arrangement, but I had such fun reading this otherwise. I truthfully rarely got bored while reading Yes, Chef and I enjoyed seeing all the small events the main characters went through with each other!

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎‎ The pacing for this book was decent, not too fast but not too slow, which allowed for a realistic timeline with not only the development of the restaurant but also the development of Poppy and Jack’s feelings. Albeit there was a lot of instant lust from both characters, it took months for their chemistry to truly bloom which had me extremely pleased with the lack of instant-love. The tension was okay, it wasn’t spectacular but at least it didn’t feel absolutely absent? I did really enjoy Poppy and Jack’s banter which was introduced on the very first pages. Yes, at times Jack specifically could just be straight up mean when it came to their back and forth, but aside from that their banter was mostly amusing.

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎‎ My one big problem with their relationship was the smut. I don’t think there were that many spicy scenes, the problem was how long it lasted when said scenes did occur. I also wasn’t a fan of the friends with benefits trope being implemented, which is what caused the lengthy spice, but then again I’ve never been a fan of said trope. Other than the smut though I really enjoyed the main character’s dynamic! The sunshine x grumpy thing they had going on was adorable and I loved seeing how they slowly warmed up to each other despite their different personalities. They definitely could’ve had some better communication, especially near the end, but the way they helped each other heal from their respective insecurities was really compelling.

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎‎ As much as I liked their dynamic, the main characters individually had some problems. Don’t get me wrong, they kept me intrigued in them and their stories throughout the entire book, but some of their actions were sort of iffy. Like Poppy bringing up a sensitive topic in the middle of sex for no reason or Jack constantly criticizing Poppy when he didn’t truly know her yet. They still had great personalities and I did like them, but they weren’t perfect characters by any means. I did really love the ADHD representation in both Poppy and Jack though! Their stories were enticing and I enjoyed seeing the depth each of them got when it came to their differing family situations. Like I said before, the depth didn’t emotionally destroy me, but it was sufficient enough to allow for a captivating time while reading. I’m also very grateful we got to see how they each got closure with their family problems rather than it being forgotten about.

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎‎ The writing did take some getting used to, it felt like a lot of sentences were longer than they had to be, but once I immersed myself in the book it was so easy to read! Yes, there were undoubtedly extremely cringey moments that had me wincing, but I enjoyed how hooked I was by Yes, Chef in the end. Also, the writing was so descriptive when it came to food and I adored it! I’ve never heard of half of the things made in this book, but I have to admit the foods were so beautifully illustrated in vibrant detail. I also really liked seeing enjoyable side characters that all helped Poppy and Jack. Kiara and Chester, two of the side character’s, were so adorable and entertaining! At times the writing could get repetitive, but this was such a cute, fun summer read.

౨ৎ Poppy Winfield.

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎‎ As much as she gave me second-hand embarrassment, I really liked Poppy’s character. Like I said before, the ADHD representation was so interesting and I loved seeing how she adapted to the difficulties it brought her. Her character was illustrated so vibrantly and I really enjoyed the sunshine-y vibes she brought to the book. She was kind to everyone who deserved it but didn’t hesitate to put anyone unworthy of her kindness in their place. Yes, she had me cringing and annoyed a few times, but she was also super interesting! I loved how she finally found her passion without her family’s help.

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎‎ The depth she got wasn’t extraordinarily perfect but I honestly don’t think it needed to be. Despite having what looks like a perfect life, Poppy still experienced realistic problems and the turmoil it caused her was described greatly. I didn’t really relate to her at all, but I was still able to understand why she felt the way she did thanks to the writing. Also, I loved that the author didn’t make her character solely about her ADHD. Instead it was a small part of her big, bubbly personality. We learned about her interests which I liked and although she was similar to a lot of other sunshine-y FMC’s, I think she got a decent amount of individuality.

౨ৎ Jack Hartman.

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎‎ I might be the only one, but I didn’t hate Jack’s character. He was certainly rude for no reason at times, and I truthfully didn’t love him, but I think he had a decent amount of character development to make up for it. Unfortunately this development didn’t really happen until the very end of this book, but he also had his kind moments woven throughout the story. Him baking Poppy pop-tarts from scratch after she mentioned them once was really cute! He didn’t give me much second-hand embarrassment, but he was sadly as as cringey as Poppy. His little knife tattoos had me cringing from the first chapter. However, I do love seeing MMC’s with interesting jobs, so I guess that can make up for his chef-related tattoos?

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎‎ I think the depth he got was, alike to Poppy’s, good enough to help me understand the way he acted. Maybe it’s because I cry over the smallest things, but I did tear up when it came to his relationship with Sal. Seeing how Sal’s death affected him and how he later healed from it was so endearing, I was completely addicted to their storyline. Jack finally getting the family he never fully got was so refreshing, I loved seeing his closed off, self-destructive demeanor change after Poppy entered his life. Again, he undoubtedly had his questionably rude moments, but I certainly enjoyed his character.

⤿ read: july 08 - july 15

I think a lot of people are going to absolutely adore this book!! I have to start by saying that my rating comes down to personal preference due to a few things that just didn't work for me. A 3.5 FOR ME, is still a good rating! I also want to mention that I LOVE Grace Reilly and think she's an amazing writer, but unfortunately this one didn't hit quite the same way her previous books have for me.

If you've watched The Bear and love Carmy, then you'll probably fall head over heels for Chef Jack. The story follows Jack, a chef who gets fired from his job and heads to Florida to prove himself by becoming the owner and head chef of his own restaurant. Enter Poppy, an influencer and marketing expert who's also trying to prove to her family that she's serious about her career. She agrees to help Jack put the restaurant on the map. The only problem? They can't stand each other I GIGGLE BECAUSE CLASSIC!!! 😂

I really enjoyed the storyline, the banter, and the humor throughout the book. One thing Grace does incredibly well is create characters and situations that feel very realistic and relatable. Unfortunately, some aspects of the romance and character personalities is what started to lose me as a reader while the story progressed.

Poppy could be a little frustrating at times, and she was clumsy as hell!!! I know people like that exist in real life, but wow I was cringing some times.. And Jack? He was an asshole. Like, Carmy level asshole 😭 Between the way he treated Poppy at the beginning and some of his snappy comments throughout the book, I struggled to actually like him for a good part of the story.

As for the spicy scenes, don't get me wrong I love a good dirty sex scene 🌶️ But the style and wording of some of the intimate moments just weren't for me. That though is completely a matter of personal taste, and what didn't work for me might be your favorite thing about this book!

At the end of the day, I still recommend anything Grace Reilly writes, and I know this book is going to be a hit for a lot of readers. So take this review for what it is: my personal reading experience 💕

Thank you Netgalley & Avon for my earc!

July 24, 2026
‎❝ it's as though she reached into my chest and scooped out my heart. and now it's hers for safekeeping. ❞


‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎this book single-handedly convinced me that if a tattooed chef with unresolved grief yelled at me in a professional kitchen, i would simply stand there and say, "yes, chef." my self-respect and dignity would be sautéed in garlic butter and served on a pretty platter.


₊˚꒰ ⟡ ˙ i. plot. ₊˚⊹ ꒱
‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎yes, chef follows jack hartman, a grumpy chef whose already fragile life completely implodes after a public meltdown gets him fired from a michelin-starred restaurant. at the exact same restaurant, poppy winfield, an influencer and the owner's daughter, is publicly dumped by her nba-star boyfriend.

the two reluctantly team up to reopen sailfish, the beloved florida restaurant jack inherited from his late mentor, sal. jack handles the kitchen, poppy handles the marketing, and somewhere between teaching her how to cook, renovating the restaurant, and arguing every five minutes, they accidentally catch feelings.


₊˚꒰ ⟡ ˙ ii. jack hartman. ₊˚⊹ ꒱
‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎jack, sir, have you considered smiling?

i understood why he was the way he was. he was grieving the loss of sal, drowning in guilt, and carrying enough emotional baggage to require its own checked suitcase. but my GOD this man spent the first third of the book acting like happiness personally insulted him.

that being said, i am unfortunately weak for tattooed fictional chefs. it's a character flaw. watching him slowly soften around poppy was genuinely one of my favorite parts of the book. every tiny crack in that grumpy exterior felt earned instead of magically disappearing overnight.


₊˚꒰ ⟡ ˙ iii. poppy supremacy. ₊˚⊹ ꒱
‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎POPPY YOU WILL ALWAYS BE FAMOUS. i adored her.

i loved that beneath the influencer persona was someone who desperately wanted to be taken seriously by her family instead of constantly being dismissed. watching her prove that social media marketing is an actual skill made me so irrationally happy as a marketing student. she wasn't just an influencer. she understood branding, audience engagement, storytelling, and how to get people invested in a business. she carried this restaurant on her beautifully moisturized back.


₊˚꒰ ⟡ ˙ iv. the food. ₊˚⊹ ꒱
‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ this book should honestly come with a grocery list. every chapter had me starving. every description of seafood made me hungry. every kitchen scene made me briefly consider culinary school before remembering i once burned water somehow.

the restaurant atmosphere was honestly one of the strongest parts of the book. you could feel the pressure of service, the chaos of the kitchen, and the love that went into rebuilding sailfish. the setting feel incredibly immersive for me.


₊˚꒰ ⟡ ˙ v. romance. ₊˚⊹ ꒱
‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ the banter was genuinely fun. like, poppy would say something slightly unhinged and jack would respond like a man actively trying not to throw a knife across the room. there were moments where their dialogue had me smiling into my book like an idiot, especially when they were sniping at each other while also clearly clocking each other's attractiveness in real time.

the forced proximity was actually really well done though. them being stuck together in the restaurant, constantly in each other's space, sharing a kitchen where everything is sharp and flammable and emotionally charged? that part worked. and the cooking lessons?? i ate that up. living and working together also gave us some really good tension.

jack, specifically, was also a bit hard for me to fully warm up to at first. i understood his grief, his anger, his whole "i live in the kitchen and emotionally repress everything" thing, but there were stretches where i wanted just a little more softness earlier on. his emotional arc was strong, and i did appreciate the growth, but i think i needed more consistent glimpses of vulnerability to fully buy into the romance hitting that top-tier level. so yeah, very good meal, slightly under-seasoned obsession.

also, one thing i really appreciated was the adhd representation. both jack and poppy have adhd, but they experience it so differently that it never felt repetitive. jack throws himself so completely into the kitchen that everything else disappears. poppy's brain is constantly bouncing between ideas, conversations, and projects at lightning speed.

i also loved that neither of them had to "grow out of it" for the romance to work. they simply found someone who understood how the other's brain worked instead of trying to change it. as someone whose attention span sucks ass, i appreciated seeing two characters whose brains weren't treated like problems to solve. they were messy, forgetful, impulsive, hyperfocused, occasionally chaotic, and still completely deserving of love.


₊˚꒰ ⟡ ˙ vi. conclusion. ₊˚⊹ ꒱
overall, yes, chef was a fun, summery romance with great food, an immersive restaurant setting, a lovable heroine, and enough sexual tension to keep me turning the pages.

— 3.5 stars. ⋆˚☆˖°.ᐟ

This was such an unexpected cute surprise. Jack is a chef trying to rebuild his life and reputation, while Poppy is figuring out who she is beyond the influencer persona everyone has already decided she is. Throw them together, add a restaurant, a whole lot of tension, and…yeah things get interesting 🤣

I honestly loved the restaurant setting, especially because I’ve worked in a restaurant before. Getting to see all those behind-the-scenes details made the whole thing feel extra fun for me because I could actually picture so much of it. There was something weirdly satisfying about reading the kitchen chaos and knowing exactly how some of that environment feels 🙂‍↕️

And Poppy and Jack??? The grumpy x sunshine was GRUMPY. like aggressively grumpy 😂 But honestly, I think Poppy needed someone like Jack. She had spent so much of her life without much structure or anyone really pushing her to be better, and while I did think Jack could be a little too strict sometimes, I ultimately loved seeing how much she flourished because of that challenge. Watching Poppy slowly realize that she was capable of so much more than being an influencer was probably my favorite part of the book. Her growth felt genuine, and she was easily my favorite character👏🏼

I also really appreciated Jack’s journey. He had to confront the mistakes he made in the past and realize that punishing himself forever wasn’t the same thing as taking responsibility.Seeing him finally work through that guilt and allow himself some closure (and eventually happiness) was really satisfying 😌

My one bigger complaint was the romance itself. I wanted MORE softness. There were some genuinely sweet moments between them, but it felt like almost every emotional moment, reconciliation, or post-fight interaction eventually turned physical. And while this book is definitely spicy, I found myself wishing we could just sit in the romantic tension sometimes. I also cringed a little through some of those sex scenes because they were just... i don't even know. I didn't like some of them leave it at that🤣

Still, I had such a good time with this one. The character growth, the restaurant atmosphere, and especially Poppy made it a really enjoyable read. And we absolutely cannot forget little Gator because what a CUTIE 🐈‍⬛💝

favorite quotes ↓

"Poppy’s hair is like sunshine. Egg yolks. Lemon zest. Corn after it’s been roasted, all sweet and summery. It holds hundreds of shades, same as her jeweled eyes. I bet it’s silky, like softened butter."

"She’s wearing bright red lipstick, glossy and perfect like apple skin. Her mouth looks good enough to nibble on. If she kissed me, she’d leave marks.
I’d very much like to earn those temporary tattoos."

"This is the place where I fell in love with food, and then fell in love with a woman who resists every category, definition, and expectation. There’s no one in the world like Poppy Winfield."

I think I enjoyed the premise of the book more than the actual story. I don't think this book was for me, but it can definitely work for someone else. I wasn't fond of the overly done quirkiness and humor, along with the over-the-top tropes and the very stereotypical characters. It's definitely a fun read, and I think it does a great job illustrating how it feels to not belong. But did not hit the mark for me. Also, for some reason, I found it funny as hell that he has knives tattooed on his knuckles lol.

We follow Poppy and Jack as they navigate their emotional connection and their restaurant in the small hometown Jack is from. Poppy comes from a successful food industry family in which she feels like she does not really fit in. She finds her talent in social media. When Jack is humiliated after he is let go from his current job at Poppy's father's restaurant, Poppy decides to follow him in hopes that their aspiration of opening a restaurant together succeeds. Poppy uses her social media presence to try to build a good reputation for the restaurant, while Jack is the face of the project. Their relationship starts off with the usual dislike of each other, and through close proximity, it's a whole "I liked you the entire time."

I actually disliked the entire relationship. Poppy was a bit much at times (although I liked how the author wrote her character growth at the end), and Jack was just mean and condescending to her the entire time. And man, they just do not have any chemistry, it's just a constant physical attraction.

I really do think someone else will enjoy this book better than me! I might have had really high expectations and was let down, but this one just didn't do anything for me. It is a fun and quick read, though, kinda like a palate cleanser.

Yes, Chef serves up an enemies-to-lovers romance with plenty of heat—both in the kitchen and between its leads.

When celebrity chef Jack is fired by his mentor (who also happens to be Poppy’s father) and influencer Poppy goes viral for all the wrong reasons after a spectacularly public breakup, neither of them is in a good place. There’s obviously history between them, though Grace Reilly wisely lets those details simmer before revealing exactly what happened.

Jack and Poppy immediately feel like opposites. Jack is the tattooed, cynical chef with all the brooding confidence romance readers expect from the fictional “bad boy.” Poppy is the privileged heiress to a restaurant dynasty whose razor-sharp humor is often aimed at her own disastrous love life. She cries; he broods. They both know exactly which role they’re supposed to play.

When circumstances force them to work together restoring a struggling Florida restaurant, the sparks aren’t limited to Jack’s cooking. Their constant bickering gradually transforms into playful, flirtatious banter, and watching that shift unfold is one of the book’s biggest strengths. Poppy’s running commentary had me laughing more than once, while Jack’s increasingly desperate attempts to convince himself he isn’t falling for her made for an entertaining counterpoint.

One aspect I especially appreciated was how much care went into the restaurant itself. This isn’t simply a backdrop for the romance. The mouthwatering food descriptions will leave you hungry, the renovation of the aging building is surprisingly engaging, and Poppy’s work developing the restaurant’s marketing reminds readers that influencing is more than simply posting attractive photos online. Both characters grow as they rebuild the business—and themselves.

The audiobook is equally enjoyable overall. Samantha Summers perfectly captures Poppy’s blend of embarrassment, optimism, and wit. Troy Duran’s deep, gravelly voice is ideal for Jack and adds plenty of appeal to his chapters. His female voices aren’t quite as convincing, though that’s less a criticism than a reminder of how difficult that transition is for any narrator with such a naturally low register. It’s one of the reasons I always enjoy full-cast productions or dual narration woven throughout each chapter, even if those formats aren’t always practical.

The romance itself doesn’t reinvent many familiar tropes, but the restaurant setting gives it a fresh flavor. At times it felt like The Bear had been blended with a romantic comedy. Beneath all the witty arguments and growing attraction is an undercurrent of frustration, ambition, and longing as two people carrying plenty of emotional baggage slowly figure out who they want to become.

If you enjoy enemies-to-lovers romances, restaurant settings, witty banter, and enough culinary detail to make you crave your next meal, Yes, Chef is an entertaining recipe that delivers.

Thank you to NetGalley and HarperAudio Adult for providing an advanced listener copy in exchange for my honest review. All opinions are my own.

A fun, quick, spicy rom-com!!

What to expect -
🥪 Chef MMC × influencer FMC
🥪 Grumpy x sunshine
🥪 Witty banter
🥪 Opposites attract
🥪 Hate to love (more like reluctant allies to lovers)
🥪 ADHD representation
🥪 Self-discovery
🥪 Small-town vibes (close-knit community)
🥪 Female friendship

Chef Jack Hartman has a public meltdown at the elite restaurant where he's working and returns to his hometown in South Florida, the very place he once ran away from. His mentor has left him his restaurant, but Jack doesn't feel like he deserves it. On the other hand, Poppy, who's recently had her heart broken, decides it's finally time to run away from her own life too. She wants to prove to her family that she can handle things on her own and doesn't always need them to clean up her messes. Her plan? Revamp the restaurant Jack has inherited from his mentor, prove to her family that she's capable of much more than just being a beauty influencer, and help Jack get his career back on track.

This was such an easy audiobook to get through, and the narrators made the experience even better. That being said, it just didn't hit all the right notes for me.

Our MMC, Jack, was a tough guy to like because he was constantly grumpy and irritable. Even the smallest things Poppy did seemed to annoy him, and he'd lash out at her, only to regret it and apologize later. While I understood where a lot of his resentment toward the world, his past, and even Poppy came from, it still felt like he had an unnecessarily short temper at times, and that just didn't sit right with me. What disappointed me even more was that, even after he and Poppy bonded over their ADHD and how overwhelming it can be to constantly have so many thoughts racing through your mind, he'd still lose his temper with her so easily.

But he wasn't all flaws either. He genuinely celebrated Poppy's accomplishments and always made her feel proud of how far she'd come. He even attempted to bake one of her favorite desserts after hearing her talk about a special memory attached to it, even though he isn't a baker. Like... isn't that the sweetest thing?!!🥹 I also loved watching him slowly soften as he fell for her. He became more open to listening to her opinions about the restaurant and even welcomed her ideas for the menu. (And trust me, convincing a chef who's fiercely protective of their kitchen to accept someone else's ideas is no easy feat. 😭) Unfortunately... he completely ruined a lot of that character growth by refusing to open up when it mattered most. This man listens to Poppy, comforts her, protects her, and does everything for her... yet he stays emotionally guarded until the very end. I just wish he'd opened up about his feelings and his trust issues much earlier. 😭😭

On the other hand, I absolutely adored Poppy and wouldn't hesitate to fight for her because she's the sweetest, bubbliest, and most lovable person🥹💖 She constantly feels like she's never enough, and because of her ADHD and the struggles she had with academics, she's always felt inferior to her sister. Even as a successful influencer, she believes people only admire her because of her wealthy family and her appearance, and that nobody truly sees her.

When she arrives in Florida to help Jack, she throws herself wholeheartedly into making the restaurant succeed. Even though Jack treats her terribly at first, she sticks with it, learns everything from working the front of the restaurant to helping in the kitchen, and even contributes ideas for the menu by suggesting different ingredient and sauce combinations. Watching her grow from an insecure rich girl into a woman who could practically run a restaurant from the ground up made me so incredibly proud of her.🥺💖

Another character I absolutely loved was Kiara, Jack's mentor's daughter. She welcomed Poppy with so much warmth and kindness, and despite everything that had happened between Jack and her father, she was willing to forgive him and give him a second chance. I really admired her for that.

Now... the other thing that didn't work for me, besides our MMC, was the spice. 😫 Tell me why every single time they got close after their first kiss... it immediately led to sex.😭 I completely understand that they're attracted to each other and couldn't keep their hands off one another, but almost every sweet moment in the kitchen or during their brainstorming sessions ended with them making out. And it wasn't just a page or two - it went on for pages.😭😭

Personally, I just wish some of those moments had remained soft, romantic moments instead of always ending in the bedroom. It often took away from the sweetness of Jack complimenting Poppy or doing thoughtful things for her because the scene almost always shifted into spice. This could totally just be a me thing, though, because I have a pretty low tolerance for spice in romance, so definitely take my opinion with a grain of salt. 🤭

Overall, if you're looking for a fast-paced rom-com where two complete opposites work together to save a small-town restaurant, slowly fall in love, and share plenty of steamy moments along the way, I'd definitely recommend giving this one a try.

Poppy Winfield is a cheerful, lively, sunny social media influencer.
Not a proper job for someone who belongs to the Winfield Restaurant Empire family.
Always controlled by her parents, especially her dad Douglas.
She will never be like the perfect and successful older sister Julia.
But she wants her dad's approval!

Jack Hartman is a talented, brilliant, grumpy, rude, chef that works in Douglas's "Pastiche" restaurant.
Every time he meets Poppy, they clash with each other and he always calls her Princess, because she has a family who cares about her.
But someone like Jack, who was abandoned at birth and has a troubled past in the foster system, doesn't know that "(...) a castle can still be a cage."

On the day Jack is fired by Douglas, a critic, that is always bringing his work down, returns one of his dishes to the kitchen and he has a meltdown in front of all the guests.
At the same time, in the same place, Poppy's boyfriend is breaking up with her because she is not wife material, offering her in return expensive pity jewels that she shoves back to him.
What a scandal!
So she and Jack end up in the most sleezy bar drinking their sorrows, him telling her Sal was is mentor when he was 15 years-old and teached him everything he knew about cooking, before he went to culinary school and never returned!
That he left him his restaurant "Sailfish" on Diamond Bay, a small town on the coast of Florida.
Poppy suggests that he should run it, and show her father how good he is and he will realize the huge mistake he made!
And she will help him with all her contacts she has in social media!

Sal left his house to his daughter Kiara and to him, besides the restaurant, a little houseboat where he would live.
And as her family is pitying her for the break up, Poppy tells them she's going to work with Jack promoting is restaurant.

Jack tells her that if she wants to promote a restaurant she needs to know it from every angle.
So she'll have to learn how to cook.
They are not partners.
He is her boss and he chooses the personnel and the menu.
He doesn't like her but he needs her.

The building is so dirty that almost looks derilit and first they'll have to clean it.
She must always answer him when he orders her to do something by "Yes, Chef" (hence the title of the book) and "Heard" because it lets him know she understood!
If she's in, to be there the next day at 4: a.m.!
And the cleaning continues for several days.
Jack needs noise to focus but she can't stand the music anymore, so when he's not looking, she finds his phone in the office and a tube of pills with is name on it that she knows well for ADHD.
He's neurodivergent.
When he catches her she tells him she is too, and it makes him go softer on her!
His infuriating beyond belief but know they have something in common.
When she goes home she finds a black white cat at the marina that she will name Alligator (Gator), takes it to Kiara Vet clinic and they bond instantly.
She made a friend!

Poppy needs a name to start the restaurant account in Instagram and he chooses FABLE because Sal used to say "Cooking is just another form of story telling!"

He starts to teach Poppy how to cook, beginning with chopping onions.
When she does it right he praises her.
She's stunned!

Douglas phones Jack because Poppy isn't answering her phone, and if his new restaurant is a success they can talk again about the promotion to his new restaurant, but only if he takes care of Poppy, keeping her out of trouble.
He agrees.
Jack thinks she's charming, pretty, magnetic, likes her hair, blond like sunshine and eggs yolks!
He's got it bad!
He realizes how good she is at looking the potential in things, just like when he looks at a collection of ingredients and imagines a meal.

He is a very good teacher!
When she moans eating something he made, it takes his mind to dangerous and dirty paths!
"The expetience of the food is as important as the food itself."
The tension builds up between them, and caged between his body and the table she struggles to breathe.
Cooking the result of another lesson she continues to film when he said to stop and inadvertently she jerks away of the splattering oil and he burns his forearm and he says he can't trust a stubborn brat like her!
(I stopped breathing!!)
Everyone in her life called her that even Julia!

He decides to take a day off with her in an island near the coast, apoligizes to her, and she to Jack because she didn't want to hurt him!
She likes this relaxed version of Jack, shirtless, his tattoed chest and neck, his swim trunks low on his waist!

Then there's the cockroach and he brings her to the boathouse to stay.
It feels good to have her close but she would never stay with someone like him!
She'll be going back to her world again.
It's only temporary!

She has lots of good ideas about things to put on the menu and about the Pop-Up before opening day
But one day he can't hold himself anymore.
He kisses her with everything he's got and she kisses him back the same way!
They begin a spicy relationship, but with no kisses on the lips, she says, because they are intoxicating and dangerous!

A few bumps will happen between them until the end, but don't worry too much!
They'll both get what they want!

summary/thoughts: ⋆˚࿔
yes, chef follows jack, a talented but troubled chef who returns to his hometown after a public meltdown, and poppy, a determined social media influencer trying to prove herself. when the two reluctantly team up to revive his late mentor’s struggling restaurant, he handling the food and she handling the branding, they’re forced into close quarters despite clashing personalities. as tensions rise in the kitchen, so does the chemistry, and what starts as a strategic partnership slowly turns into something more as they both confront their pasts and figure out what they really want.

this was such an adorable and addicting read, i was honestly hooked the whole time. i will say… jack frustrated me quite a bit, especially at the beginning when we don’t fully understand his backstory. i get that he’s meant to be grumpy and dealing with a lot, but some of the way he treated poppy just didn’t sit right with me. i kept wishing he would handle situations better and communicate more clearly. but poppy really made this book for me. i loved her character so much. the youngest daughter representation was something i don’t see very often, and it actually made me feel seen in a way i wasn’t expecting. i loved watching her grow, prove herself, and step into her confidence. and the chemistry between them was so good. the tension, the back-and-forth, the slow build… it all worked really well and kept me invested!

overall, this was a fun and emotional read with great character dynamics. even though jack tested my patience at times, the story as a whole was engaging and easy to get lost in

── .✦ characters 𓂃˖ ࣪⊹

poppy winfield: 𖦹₊ ⊹
poppy was honestly my favorite part of this book. she’s bubbly, underestimated, and constantly trying to prove that she’s more than what people assume about her. i loved seeing the youngest daughter representation through her character, it felt so real at times. she carries this pressure of not being taken seriously, but still pushes herself to grow and step outside her comfort zone. watching her become more confident and sure of herself throughout the story was so satisfying

jack hartman: 𖦹₊ ⊹
jack is very much the classic grumpy, closed-off chef dealing with grief and anger, which i understood… but he definitely frustrated me. especially in the beginning, when we don’t fully know his story, some of his behavior towards poppy just felt unfair. he has his moments, and you can see the depth underneath, but i do wish he handled certain situations better. he grew on me over time, but he tested my patience more than once. i had to stop reading at times just to not get mad. but towards the end, everything just made sense as to why he kept running away. he really deserved the biggest hug.

── .✦ quotes 𓂃˖ ࣪⊹
“I love you, Poppy. You’re brilliant and clever and mine. On and off the desert island.”

“I love you, Poppy. I—god, I love you so much it terrifies me. You make me want to be a better man. A happy man.”

This is the place where I fell in love with food, and then fell in love with a woman who resists every category,definition, and expectation. There’s no one in the world like Poppy Winfield, and she wanted me, and I set it all on fire just as neatly and completely as I did more than a decade ago, when I could’ve had a family and chose to run. When I told myself I needed to leave for the good of my career.

this book was everything i’d hoped it would be and more!! i have been chomping at the bit to read this since the moment i saw graces announcement and even more so after getting to yap about it a little with her at a book fest last year!!

everything about this book was perfection from start to finish, i couldnt stop giggling and kicking. my feet in the beginning when poppy and jack were at each others throats and absolutely adored the way the dynamic between the two of them started to slowly shift into friendship and then into real feelings for one another.

the chemistry between jack and poppy was absolutely insane, i think this is my most favorite banter within a romance book i’ve read in a long time. the way these two gave zero fucks about being at each others throats and teasing one another is actually one of the highlights of my year thus far, i can only imagine how much fun these two are going to be when brought to live via audiobook!!

this book while at its core is a cute summery romcom it also had the most amazing emotional depth to it. neither of the characters are perfect but do they try damn hard to be for one another and it was so beautiful to watch jacks journey through grieving and the way poppy was always there when he let down his guard more and more. the way this book handles ADHD rep with so much love and care and the way we get to see the differences of how it affects both poppy and jack in different ways and bringing attention how hard women have to fight for themselves to get diagnoses. the way jack helps reassure poppy that theres just simply nothing wrong with her like she believes there is and really fights for her to believe in herself and try new things as scary as they may be and that she is worth everything and more.

there are so many tender moments through out this book that just melted my heart completely and it was just so easy to fall in love with poppy, jack, gator, kiara, chester, fable and though we only get to know sal posthumously the way he loved was so visceral he was very easy to adore.

this book was just entirely too good and too much fun, i cannot wait to rotate it into my tbr constantly when i get my hands on the audiobook upon release. diamond bay is a place i will forever love to revisit.

I was hooked from the first sentence - literally!

Grace Reilly instantly captured an undeniable tension between Poppy and Jack. All it took was a shrimp to the head 🍤🧑🏻‍🍳😂

Honestly though, this book was SO much better than I hoped for. I was drawn in by the synopsis but stayed for the chemistry. This was such a unique spin on an enemies-to-lovers romance that also included many of my favourite tropes including grumpy x sunshine, forced proximity, workplace dynamics.

💖 👑 x 🖤 🔪

If you’re looking for one last summer read - this is it! Pure rom-com GOLD 💛

After getting fired from an elite Manhattan restaurant, Chef Jack Hartman reluctantly returns to his hometown in Florida. Poppy, his former boss’s daughter, is also desperate for an escape. The determined social media influencer, is publicly dumped and running from her disapproving family. With both of their reputations in ruins, they strike up a deal to bring Jack’s unloved restaurant from his childhood back to life. Meanwhile, Poppy is sure she can use her infamous social media skills to put this East Coast shack on the map. Both trying to win Poppy’s dad’s approval, they work together to create a new hotspot. But as tension rises, will their plan all go up in flames? ❤️‍🔥

Poppy is an irresistible FMC. I couldn’t help but fall in love with her and root for her from beginning to end. Sure she’s a bit of a princess but her like-ability is undeniable. I loved how much her character developed over the course of the story. At the beginning, Jack sees her as a beautiful blonde who is utterly infuriating. But she proves herself to be so much more than a spoiled ‘brat’. Her determination and passion is what sets her apart. I admired her tenacity which made her easy to root for. She brought so much light and enthusiasm to this book, with a big bright personality, she was a breath of fresh air. Love you Pop Rocks 💖

Who knew I had a thing for tattooed chefs? Jack certainly confirmed that fact for me 🤭 Despite his compulsion to be grumpy this man had charm by the bucketload! His banter was off the charts. But what surprised me most was the complexities of his character. I was very impressed by the depth of emotion Reilly put into all of her characters.

This enemies to lovers arc was so on point 👌🏽 add in the forced proximity of the kitchen - including teaching Poppy to cook - and BAM 💥 - a situation that could blow up in flames at any given moment 🔥 The tension between these two was sky high, and I was thoroughly entertained during the slow-burn waiting process. With a dash of too many cooks in the kitchen, the emotional strain is HIGH. Past truths bubble at the surface, but they can’t stay simmering forever… 👀

I loved to see the ADHD representation here in BOTH MC’s. It’s not just young boys that struggle with neurodivergence, females have it too and are often diagnosed much later in life. I was impressed with how Reilly portrayed many aspects of how neurodivergence can effect the lives of the individual and those around them.

I have to mention the side characters in this story. They added a real sense of warmth and found family feels to the book. I particularly loved Kiara. She played a key role in how the story played out, and it definitely wouldn’t be the same without her. I kinda wish we could get a book just for her and Chester. As for the others, there were many to love, but I also lowkey hate Poppy’s dad 😒 He was a persistent headache, and despite putting things right in the end, he was the source of many problems.

Overall, I have to say it: 'Chef's kiss!’ 🤌🏽 I loved the originality of this book. Reilly did a fantastic job at creating multi-layered characters, a vibrant setting, and strong vibes. If you’re looking for a new spin on a slow-burning romance this is definitely one to try. I will definitely be reading more of Reilly’s books soon!

4 🌟🌟🌟🌟

⤿ Thank you to Avon for the arc through netgalley in exchange for an honest review!

i am truly the saddest person alive that i did not like this book...it sounds SO delectable and cute but unfortunately it just did not hit the right marks for me 🤧 i'm especially sad because so many people have been loving this online and i wish i was able to jump on that bandwagon. while i did not like this overall, there is definitely praise that should be directed at the food pieces in this book. i'm not a chef, but i DO love cooking and baking so i was really excited to see how the cooking part of this book would play out. frequently Jack and Poppy make new dishes, try flavors together and describe these dishes in really interesting ways. i loved seeing this part, but unfortunately it was not able to carry the book for me.

my biggest issue with this book was Jack Hartman as a character. it's revealed through the book that he grew up in foster care, was in juvie and had a rough childhood until he landed with this restaurant owner and his daughter. he ended up growing up with them and then leaving when this owner said he wanted him to take over the restaurant, later regretting it as the owner died before he could say goodbye (as he never came back). i totally understand that all those experiences definitely have an impact on a person, and Jack had a really hard life he is definitely afforded a high level of grace and empathy. but those explain his actions, they don't excuse them. throughout almost the entire book he's just straight up mean to Poppy, he snaps at her like she's supposed to know everything about a kitchen when she is LEARNING. he doesn't apologize and also is just the most avoidant person ever. i get it, he needs to learn how to not do that, but he continually hurts others around him by doing this (knowing full well he is and not trying to change). i got annoyed with him pretty quickly, as i understood why he was the way he was but was unable to excuse his actions because he was just rude and hurtful to those around him.

Poppy herself was a fine main character, she was sweet and a bit ditzy at times, but she grew up kind of sheltered. what made her compelling was despite not knowing anything about cooking, she was super willing to learn and always try things herself- even if Jack was saying she couldn't do it. i did really enjoy this about her and i loved her positive attitude as well. she goes through some tough things in this book as well, but she chooses to be as kind as possible and i appreciated it. also, finding a stray cat and naming him Gator because she's in florida is hilarious. i approve.

i could see why the two of them could have a romantic connection, mostly built upon being polar opposites but i never felt there was really time for the tension to simmer. they went from fighting, to suddenly both thinking about what each other looks like under their clothes. it was about halfway through the book, but i needed more time in between for me to fully believe in their romance. not just jump from one extreme to the other.

this was unfortunately just not for me, i really wanted to love it and get attached to these characters but it was not meant to be. though if you enjoy food descriptions and a touch of romance, this would be a book to check out for you!

❤️‍🔥🔥 Yes, Chef 🔥❤️‍🔥

The spice in this book was 🔥🔥
It shows up early, and it's so very satisfying! But the author also did a fantastic job with the relationship building between both MCs. The emotional relationship was a slow build up and equally satisfying.

Both of them are carrying a lot when it comes to family. Jack is dealing with grief after losing his mentor, someone who was basically family, while also trying to figure out how to move forward and redefine his relationship with his adopted sister.

Poppy is constantly underestimated by her parents and compared to her “perfect” sister, and you can really feel how much that weighs on her. There is a clear lack of respect and trust from her dad that really shapes how she sees herself.

I loved the ending. This is easily one of my favorites from the year! Also… I need this audiobook immediately.
